title: Thorn and Choir
premise: Yara Hartwell has spent ten years hiding his storm-calling in Thornvale, a valley warded against magic where exiles grow old forgetting who they were. When the usurper Queen Vessia announces a realm-wide hunt and her hunters breach the valley's wards, Yara flees with a stolen ledger revealing that the court beneath the mountain buys souls—and that his sister's soul was sold there years ago, fueling the Queen's armies. Joined by Sef, a disgraced royal choirmaster whose songs can unbind what magic has sealed, Yara crosses the free cities gathering allies as the Queen's armies close in. In the mountain's depths he must choose between reclaiming his sister's soul and shattering the choir that powers the Queen's conquest; he chooses both, at the cost of his own memories of her, ending the hunt but leaving him a stranger to the only family he had left.
about_author: Beatrix Crane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging confiscated letters in a coastal city before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people the law forgot, and claims her best ideas arrive during thunderstorms.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Ten years after his exile, Yara tends goats and suppresses every flicker of storm in his blood, while the valley's wards slowly erode his memories of his sister Lira. When a ward-stone cracks during a freak hailstorm, he feels magic leak back in like an old wound reopening. Emotional beat: the ache of a life half-remembered.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Mill
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A crown crier arrives with the Queen's edict: all gifted persons to be surrendered or hunted. The valley elders vote to comply, and Yara realizes his neighbors' silence is a death sentence. He packs in the night, taking only his mother's storm-glass pendant. Emotional beat: betrayal by the safe place.

chapters.title: The Hunter in the Wheat
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A soul-hunter named Corvane catches Yara at the valley's edge; in desperation Yara calls his first true storm in a decade, killing the man's hounds and revealing himself. He escapes but now bears a hunter's brand-scar that will let Corvane track him anywhere. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration intertwined.

chapters.title: A Choirmaster's Debt
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. In the free city of Aldermist, Sef, once the Queen's choirmaster, recognizes the brand-scar's meaning and intercepts Yara. He confesses he trained the soul-choir that powers Vessia's armies before fleeing his complicity. He offers Yara the ledger he stole on his way out. Emotional beat: guilt seeking redemption.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Reading the ledger by candlelight, Yara finds Lira's name—sold by their own father to pay debts—bound to the choir beneath the mountain. His memories of her sharpen painfully now that magic runs free in him again. He vows to reach the court. Emotional beat: grief transformed into purpose.

chapters.title: Saltmarket Bargains
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. To cross the Queen's blockade, Sef bargains with a smuggler-queen, trading a song that unbinds sealed cargo-holds in exchange for passage. Yara distrusts the arrangement; Sef argues that justice outside the law is still justice. Emotional beat: friction between principle and necessity.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Straits
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The smuggler ship is boarded by the Queen's navy, and Yara must call a storm to save them, drowning sailors he can see drowning. He saves the ship and hates himself for it. Corvane's brand burns hotter—he is close. Emotional beat: the cost of power used well.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Muster
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. In the free city of Vhal, Yara and Sef find the cities' council paralyzed by fear of the Queen's armies. Yara, against Sef's caution, demonstrates his storm-calling publicly, galvanizing some delegates and painting a target on all of them. Emotional beat: hope that is also recklessness.

chapters.title: What the Brand Remembers
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Corvane corners Yara in the council archives, but instead of fighting, offers him a deal: surrender the ledger and the Queen will spare the free cities a season. Yara refuses and learns Corvane was once valley-born too, an exile who chose the crown. Emotional beat: recognition of the man he could become.

chapters.title: Ashes of Vhal
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Vessia's vanguard strikes Vhal early; the council's cowardice dooms the city. Yara and Sef escape through burning streets carrying the ledger and a handful of refugees, including a gifted child named Oren who clings to Yara like a son. Emotional beat: failure, and responsibility born from it.

chapters.title: The Road Beneath
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The refugees take the old mining road toward the mountain, and Oren's uncontrolled gift nearly betrays them to a patrol. Yara teaches the boy to hold a storm inside himself the way he learned—by remembering grief. Emotional beat: reluctant mentorship, tenderness hard-won.

chapters.title: Sef's Requiem
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. At a wayshrine, Sef plays the requiem he composed for the souls he helped bind, and Yara finally forgives him—or begins to. Sef reveals the choir can be unbound only from within, by a voice the bound souls once trusted. Emotional beat: absolution neither man believes he deserves.

chapters.title: The Queen's Summons
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Summoned before Vessia, Corvane is ordered to bring Yara alive, for the Queen wants a storm-caller's soul for her crown. Corvane sees in her hunger what he might have become and begins quietly sabotaging his own hunt. Emotional beat: a hunter's conscience waking.

chapters.title: Gate of the Mountain Court
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara, Sef, and Oren reach the mountain's gate, where entry is sold in memories: each traveler pays a year. Yara pays a year of Lira, and feels her fading further. Sef's court credentials get them past the wardens. Emotional beat: sacrifice as toll, memory as currency.

chapters.title: The Choir Below
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Descending through galleries of suspended soul-lanterns, Sef hears the bound choir singing the Queen's war-march and recognizes individual voices, including Lira's. He teaches Yara the counter-song in whispers, knowing discovery means death. Emotional beat: awe and horror in equal measure.

chapters.title: Lira
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara reaches his sister's lantern and speaks to what remains of her; she remembers only the valley, only him, dimly. To free her he must sing the counter-song while she still knows his face—but the Queen's wardens arrive, alerted by Corvane's false report meant to save Yara's life. Emotional beat: reunion that is also farewell.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Crown
chapters.summary: Vessia's POV (interlude). The Queen confronts the intruders, revealing the crown is fed by the choir and that she sold her own memories to wear it. She offers Yara Lira's freedom in exchange for his storm-soul. Emotional beat: the villain as a mirror—duty devouring love.

chapters.title: Counter-Song
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara refuses the bargain; Sef begins the counter-song as wardens close in. Corvane turns his blade on the wardens, buying seconds with his life. Yara takes Lira's lantern in both hands and sings the unbinding as the choir's harmony fractures. Emotional beat: defiant love against impossible odds.

chapters.title: The Mountain Sings Back
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The choir breaks free, and the released souls' grief becomes a storm the mountain cannot contain. Yara channels it outward, shattering Vessia's crown and the army's binding—but the unbinding demands payment, and his memories of Lira are the price the song takes. Emotional beat: triumph and loss in a single breath.

chapters.title: After the Fall
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Vessia, unbound from her crown, wanders the ruins unremembering; the armies falter as their binding fails. Sef carries a hollow-eyed Yara and the freed souls' lanterns out of the collapsing court, with Oren holding the ledger. Emotional beat: exhausted survival, the war won quietly.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Gate
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Lira, freed and whole, finds Yara on the mountain road—but he does not know her face. She tells him their story as they walk, and he chooses to let her, believing love can be rebuilt from testimony. Emotional beat: sorrow braided with fragile, deliberate hope.

chapters.title: Thorn and Choir
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A year later, the free cities stand; Yara, Sef, Lira, and Oren return to Thornvale, where the wards are broken and memory flows freely again. Yara cannot recall his sister, but when a storm rises, she stands beside him and names it beautiful. Emotional beat: home redefined—not as what you remember, but who stays.
